name: Framtid
subtitle: Future: ska, kommer att, tänker; tycker vs tror

ruleCards.title: Present tense + a time word
ruleCards.rule: The easiest way to talk about the future: use the present tense and add a time word like imorgon, ikväll, på fredag or nästa vecka.
ruleCards.watch: Without a time word, the present tense usually means now or usually: Jag åker till jobbet (every day).

ruleCards.title: Ska: plans and decisions
ruleCards.rule: Use ska + infinitive for something you have planned or decided. Ska is a help verb, so the next verb is in the infinitive, with no att.
examples: Jag ska börja en kurs i januari.
I’m going to start a course in January.
Shall we go to the cinema?
ruleCards.watch: Ska can stand without a movement verb when a direction follows: Jag ska till tandläkaren. Vart ska du?

ruleCards.title: Kommer att: predictions
ruleCards.rule: Use kommer att + infinitive for what you think will happen, things nobody decides: the weather, feelings, results.
examples: Du kommer att tycka om Vasa.
Hon kommer att bli trött efter resan.
She’ll be tired after the trip.
ruleCards.watch: Don’t forget att: kommer att regna. People often drop it when speaking, but write it.

ruleCards.title: Ska or kommer att?
ruleCards.rule: Ask yourself: did someone decide this? Yes → ska. No, it’s a guess about the future → kommer att.
examples: Det kommer att bli kallt i natt.
It’s going to be cold tonight. (a prediction)
ruleCards.watch: Du ska … can sound like an order: Du ska städa ditt rum! (You will tidy your room!)

ruleCards.title: Tänker + infinitive: intentions
ruleCards.rule: Tänker + infinitive means “I intend to”. It shows what you have made up your mind to do.
examples: I’m going to quit smoking. (I intend to)
Vad tänker du göra i sommar?
What are you planning to do this summer?
ruleCards.watch: No att here: Jag tänker resa, not tänker att resa.

ruleCards.title: Tycker, tror or tänker på?
ruleCards.rule: All three can be “think” in English. Tycker = your opinion about something you know or have tried. Tror = you believe or guess, but you’re not sure. Tänker på = thinking about someone or something.
examples: Jag tycker att filmen är bra.
I think the film is good. (my opinion)
Jag tror att det kommer att regna.
I think it’s going to rain. (a guess)
ruleCards.watch: Tycker om = like: Jag tycker om kaffe.
